edges.description: Neurohormonal (angiotensin II) activation drives cardiac fibroblast IL-11 induction, placing IL-11 receptor signalling downstream of the neurohormonal stress that promotes adverse remodeling.

Loss of control over sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release reduces systolic performance, and recessive loss-of-function variants in the gene that builds the release couplon give severe, early-onset dilated cardiomyopathy.

Each gene on this node has a reported arrhythmic or conduction phenotype: the SCN5A families presented with conduction disorder and arrhythmia, loss-of-function ABCC9 variants with Brugada and early repolarization syndromes, and the TNNI3K family with conduction system disease and atrial tachyarrhythmia.

The same variants that destabilize the action potential also produce ventricular dilatation and systolic dysfunction; the SCN5A report is explicit that the cardiac sodium channel disease spectrum extends to cardiac dilation and dysfunction.

Loss of protein synthesis, folding, targeting or clearance capacity in the cardiomyocyte produces ventricular dilatation with systolic failure; the BAG5 families showed complete penetrance and required heart transplantation.
A ventricular myocardium built by a disrupted transcriptional program underperforms; MIB1 loss arrests chamber myocardium development and prevents trabecular maturation and compaction.

edges.description: The five individuals in whom biallelic PPCS variants were identified presented with dilated cardiomyopathy, and their fibroblasts showed decreased coenzyme A.

Cardiomyocytes carrying the patient's TNNT2 R173W allele reproduce the sarcomeric disorganisation and contractile failure of this node in human cells, and the phenotype is reversed by beta-blockade or SERCA2a overexpression.
edges.limitations: The authors themselves qualify the model as recapitulating the disease phenotype only to some extent. The cardiomyocytes are developmentally immature, with mitochondria and sarcoplasmic reticulum still immature at the assay stage, and the sarcomeric defect was most pronounced in single cells and at cluster edges rather than in well-coupled tissue. The cohort is a single family and a single TNNT2 allele, so the finding does not generalise across this node's other sarcomeric and cytoskeletal genes, and no chamber-level dilatation can be observed in a dish.
edges.source: Patient-specific TNNT2 R173W iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (Clinical Trials in a Dish)

edges.description: Exposing the cardiomyocytes to a beta-adrenergic agonist applies the catecholamine arm of this node directly to the cells and unmasks a genotype-dependent vulnerability that is not apparent at baseline.
edges.limitations: This is an acute pharmacological stimulus applied to isolated cardiomyocytes. It reproduces the receptor-level consequence of sympathetic drive but not neurohormonal activation as a disease process: there is no sympathetic nervous system, no renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis, no natriuretic peptide counter-regulation and no feedback loop between cardiac output and neurohormonal tone.

meta.association: Autosomal dominant causal pathogenic variant. C10orf71 encodes an intrinsically disordered, cardiomyocyte-specific protein also reported as the z-disc protein CEFIP. Frameshift variants were identified in a large family with eight affected members and in four further loss-of-function carriers across two sporadic DCM cohorts. Null cardiomyocytes lose contractile function while sarcomere structure stays intact, so the lesion is contractile rather than structural.

evidence.reference_title: Frameshift variants in C10orf71 cause dilated cardiomyopathy in human, mouse, and organoid models.
evidence.snippet: We identified candidate DCM causal gene, C10orf71, in a large family with 8 patients with DCM by whole-exome sequencing. Four loss-of-function variants of C10orf71 were subsequently identified in an additional group of492 patients with sporadic DCM from 2 independent cohorts. C10orf71 was found to be an intrinsically disordered protein specifically expressed in cardiomyocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Frameshift variants in C10orf71 cause dilated cardiomyopathy in human, mouse, and organoid models.
evidence.snippet: C10orf71-null cardiomyocytes exhibited impaired contractile function with unaffected sarcomere structure. Cardiomyocytes and heart organoids derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells with C10orf71 frameshift variants also had contractile defects with normal electrophysiological activity. A rescue study using a cardiac myosin activator, omecamtiv mecarbil, restored contractile function in C10orf71-KO mice. These data support C10orf71 as a causal gene for DCM by contributing to the contractile function of cardiomyocytes.

evidence.reference_title: The novel cardiac z-disc protein CEFIP regulates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy by modulating calcineurin signaling.
evidence.snippet: Importantly, CEFIP was located at the z-disc and was up-regulated in several models of cardiomyopathy.

meta.association: Autosomal recessive causal pathogenic variant. CAP2 encodes a cyclase-associated actin cytoskeleton regulatory protein required for the kinetics of actin filament repolymerization; a homozygous splice-consensus variant in a consanguineous Bedouin family caused DCM with supraventricular tachycardia, and patient fibroblasts showed altered actin repolymerization kinetics.

evidence.reference_title: CAP2 mutation leads to impaired actin dynamics and associates with supraventricular tachycardia and dilated cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: This is the first report of a recessive deleterious mutation in CAP2 and its association with DCM in humans. The clinical phenotype recapitulates the damaging effects on the heart observed in Cap2 knockout mice including DCM and cardiac conduction disease, but not the other effects on growth, viability, wound healing and eye development. Our data underscore the importance of the proper kinetics of actin polymerization for normal function of the human heart.

A third group of DCM genes encode transcriptional and developmental regulators of the ventricular myocardium. TBX20 is a cardiac T-box transcription factor that acts with NKX2-5 and GATA4, PRDM16 is the transcription factor whose loss accounts for the cardiomyopathy of monosomy 1p36, MIB1 is the NOTCH pathway E3 ubiquitin ligase whose loss arrests trabecular maturation and compaction, and GATAD1 was mapped in a family with recessive DCM. Left ventricular noncompaction overlaps this group, reflecting arrested chamber development rather than degeneration of a formed myocardium.

evidence.snippet: Functional assays revealed that the mutant TBX20 had significantly diminished transcriptional activity. Furthermore, the mutation markedly reduced the synergistic activation of TBX20 with NKX2-5 or GATA4.

evidence.reference_title: Fine mapping of the 1p36 deletion syndrome identifies mutation of PRDM16 as a cause of cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: we describe the loss of a gene within the deletion that is responsible for the cardiomyopathy associated with monosomy 1p36, and we confirm its role in nonsyndromic left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy (LVNC) and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM).

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the NOTCH pathway regulator MIB1 cause left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: These results implicate NOTCH signaling in LVNC and indicate that MIB1 mutations arrest chamber myocardium development, preventing trabecular maturation and compaction.

nodes.description: JPH2 and RYR2 act on the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release step rather than on the contractile apparatus. JPH2 builds the junctional membrane complex that couples the t-tubule to the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and RYR2 is the release channel itself. The reported defect is a loss of control over when release terminates rather than a smaller release: the RyR2 exon-3 region associated with dilated cardiomyopathy lowers the luminal calcium threshold at which release ends and increases the fractional release.

biological_processes: regulation of sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release

evidence.reference_title: One gene, two modes of inheritance, four diseases: A systematic review of the cardiac manifestation of pathogenic variants in JPH2-encoded junctophilin-2.
evidence.snippet: we found that autosomal recessive, loss-of-function variants are associated with severe, early onset DCM, while autosomal dominant missense variants are associated with a wider range of cardiac disease, including HCM, arrhythmia, SCD, and cardiac conduction disease.

evidence.reference_title: Abnormal termination of Ca2+ release is a common defect of RyR2 mutations associated with cardiomyopathies.
evidence.snippet: The 35-residue exon-3 region of RyR2 is associated with dilated cardiomyopathy. Single-cell luminal Ca2+ imaging revealed that the deletion of the first 305 NH2-terminal residues encompassing exon-3 or the deletion of exon-3 itself markedly reduced the luminal Ca2+ threshold at which Ca2+ release terminates and increased the fractional Ca2+ release.

nodes.description: SCN5A, ABCC9 and TNNI3K act on the cardiomyocyte action potential rather than on calcium release or on the contractile apparatus. SCN5A carries the cardiac sodium current, ABCC9 is the SUR2 subunit of the cardiac KATP channel, and TNNI3K is a cardiac troponin I interacting kinase whose disease-causing variant disrupts its kinase domain. Disease in this group characteristically presents with conduction disease and arrhythmia alongside, or ahead of, ventricular dilatation.

evidence.reference_title: SCN5A mutation associated with dilated cardiomyopathy, conduction disorder, and arrhythmia.
evidence.snippet: Our findings expand the clinical spectrum of disorders of the cardiac sodium channel to include cardiac dilation and dysfunction

evidence.reference_title: Case Report: Loss-of-Function ABCC9 Genetic Variant Associated With Ventricular Fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Genetic variants in the ABCC9 gene, encoding the SUR2 auxiliary subunit from KATP channels, were previously linked with various inherited diseases. This wide range of congenital disorders includes multisystem and cardiovascular pathologies. The gain-of-function mutations result in Cantu syndrome, acromegaloid facial appearance, hypertrichosis, and acromegaloid facial features. The loss-of-function mutations in the ABCC9 gene were associated with the Brugada syndrome, early repolarization syndrome, and dilated cardiomyopathy.

evidence.reference_title: TNNI3K mutation in familial syndrome of conduction system disease, atrial tachyarrhythmia and dilated cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: revealing an unreported heterozygous missense mutation disrupting the highly conserved kinase domain in TNNI3K.

nodes.description: A second group of DCM genes act on how cardiomyocyte proteins are made, folded, delivered and cleared rather than on the contractile apparatus itself. RPL3L is a muscle-specific ribosomal protein, GET3 (ASNA1) inserts tail-anchored membrane proteins, BAG5 is a nucleotide exchange factor that activates HSC70-mediated folding, FBXO32 (atrogin-1) is the substrate-recognition subunit of an SCF ubiquitin ligase, and PLEKHM2 positions lysosomes for autophagic flux. Most are recessive and several present in the neonatal or infantile period.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in the co-chaperone protein BAG5 cause dilated cardiomyopathy requiring heart transplantation.
evidence.snippet: we identified that homozygous truncating mutations in the gene encoding Bcl-2–associated athanogene (BAG) co-chaperone 5 (BAG5) caused inherited DCM in five patients among four unrelated families with complete penetrance.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in the co-chaperone protein BAG5 cause dilated cardiomyopathy requiring heart transplantation.
evidence.snippet: BAG5 acts as a nucleotide exchange factor for heat shock cognate 71 kDa protein (HSC70), promoting adenosine diphosphate release and activating HSC70-mediated protein folding.

evidence.reference_title: FBXO32, encoding a member of the SCF complex, is mutated in dilated cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Our results indicate that abnormal SCF activity with subsequent impairment of the autophagic flux due to a novel FBXO32 mutation is implicated in the pathogenesis of DCM.

evidence.snippet: We identified compound heterozygous variants in the highly conserved ASNA1 gene (arsA arsenite transporter, ATP-binding, homolog), which encodes an ATPase required for post-translational membrane insertion of tail-anchored proteins.

nodes.description: PPCS catalyses the second of the five enzymatic steps that make coenzyme A from vitamin B5, and biallelic PPCS variants lower cellular CoA. CoA is a cofactor for a large share of cellular enzymes including those of fatty-acid handling, so this is a metabolic cofactor lesion reaching the myocardium, distinct from the sarcomeric, ion-handling, proteostatic and transcriptional routes into the same phenotype. It is also the one route here with a directly implied treatment: CoA can be made from pantethine by a route that does not use PPCS.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in PPCS, Encoding Phosphopantothenoylcysteine Synthetase, Cause Autosomal-Recessive Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Exome sequencing in five individuals from two unrelated families presenting with dilated cardiomyopathy revealed biallelic mutations in PPCS, linking CoA synthesis with a cardiac phenotype. Studies in yeast and fruit flies confirmed the pathogenicity of identified mutations. Biochemical analysis revealed a decrease in CoA levels in fibroblasts of all affected individuals.

meta.association: X-linked causal pathogenic variant. EMD encodes emerin, an inner nuclear membrane protein whose loss classically causes Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy type 1, curated separately in this knowledge base. A distinct cardiac-only phenotype exists: the c.23C>G p.Ser8Trp missense variant co-segregated with DCM in six hemizygous males aged 36 to 50 with no muscular dystrophy, with greatly reduced myocardial emerin. The authors of that study note that before it the evidence for isolated DCM as an EMD phenotype was insufficient, so this gene is recorded here as an emerging rather than an established nonsyndromic DCM gene.
